examples.title: Your first page: headings and text
examples.description: Compare the two element calls with the heading and paragraph. In your own copy, add a second paragraph and reload: one extra call creates one extra element.
examples.explanation: The Page class defines main(root). Each builder call adds a typed Source node; the integration hosts the page and Gramlot renders it.

examples.title: Text and links
examples.description: Follow the local link and compare emphasis, quoted text and the code sample. The literal <tag> remains text rather than becoming an HTML element.
examples.explanation: Follow the nested builder calls to see how text and child elements coexist. The example includes an internal anchor and literal text that is escaped rather than interpreted as markup.

examples.title: Ordered, nested and definition lists
examples.description: Match each visible list to its loop. Add one item in your own copy; the loop supplies its markup without another hand-written block.
examples.explanation: Local sequences supply the content. Loops create the repeated list items, while nesting expresses the document hierarchy.

examples.title: Semantic page
examples.description: Use Story and Notes to move between sections. Compare header, navigation, main, article and footer with the structure in the source.
examples.explanation: Header, navigation, main, article, aside and footer give the content structure; the markup stays meaningful without decoration.

examples.title: Tables with headings and totals
examples.description: Check a row total and the final totals. In your own copy, add a region to ROWS: the loop and calculations include it automatically.
examples.explanation: Loops build the table from fixed data. Caption and scoped headings describe its structure; the footer presents the totals computed before Source is built.

examples.title: Native form controls
examples.description: Fill a few native controls, then reset the form. These are browser controls; this lesson deliberately has no Data bindings.
examples.explanation: Try typing, selecting options and moving the slider. Reset restores defaults. The submit button is disabled: this example has no save endpoint or application event handlers.

examples.title: Expandable sections and progress indicators
examples.description: Open and close each question. The progress bar and meter show fixed example values; opening a question does not start a task.
examples.explanation: The browser supplies details/summary interaction. Progress and meter values are static; the example introduces no bindings or controllers.

examples.title: Draw basic SVG shapes
examples.description: Identify each of the six shapes, then match its coordinates and color to the SVG calls. Resize the preview and notice the shared viewBox.
examples.explanation: The SVG builder creates shapes within a viewBox. Coordinates determine geometry, while the shared theme supplies colors through semantic CSS variables.

examples.title: Compose an SVG scene
examples.description: Find the repeated houses, trees and flowers. Each small method receives a position; loops reuse those methods to create one scene.
examples.explanation: Helper methods build houses, trees and flowers. Loops place repeated elements, and group transformations position their local coordinates.

examples.title: Cards with icons
examples.description: Compare the cards and their SVG icons. Change a card's content in your own copy; the shared card method keeps the presentation consistent.
examples.explanation: Helpers and loops build the cards. Each × button removes its labelled Source node through the browser Builder; Gramlot updates the DOM without reloading. Reload restores the initial cards. No Data binding or server synchronization is involved.

examples.title: Static report
examples.description: Read the report from summary to detail. Follow how rows and totals become tables and charts; these are fixed sample results, not a live service.
examples.explanation: Separate methods build each section. SVG bar lengths and table cells use one local dataset, making the connection between values and geometry explicit.

examples.title: Build a complete event page
examples.description: Use the page navigation, inspect the schedule and open a question. This complete static page combines the small HTML and SVG techniques from the earlier lessons.
examples.explanation: The main method assembles named sections. Helpers and nested loops compose the schedule, speaker cards and SVG map from fixed local data.

examples.title: Text fields: live updates and labels
examples.description: Type a customer name and watch the second field follow. Open Options, turn off live editing, then type again: the shared value changes when you leave the field.

examples.title: Checkbox: a boolean value
examples.description: Toggle either newsletter checkbox. Both views and the subscription message follow one boolean; Options lets you disable editing.

examples.title: Radio group: choose one value
examples.description: Choose a delivery option and compare the stored code below. The alternative group is independent; changing one group leaves the other untouched.

examples.title: Multiline text fields
examples.description: Edit either note. Both multiline fields share the same text; Options lets you compare live editing with updates after leaving the field.

examples.title: Password fields
examples.description: Enter a made-up password in one field. The other follows while both mask the text; this is a binding example, not a sign-in form.

examples.title: Individual radio buttons
examples.description: Select Standard, Express and Pick up in turn. Their booleans are exclusive within one group; the independent choice belongs to another group.

examples.title: Choose and bind a color
examples.description: Choose a color and compare both pickers with the swatch. All three read the same color value.

examples.title: Horizontal slider: range and steps
examples.description: Move a slider or use its arrow keys. The other slider follows in steps of five; Options lets you compare live and committed updates.

examples.title: Vertical slider: orientation and values
examples.description: Move the vertical slider from bottom to top. The horizontal slider and numeric readout follow the same value from 0 to 100.

examples.title: Numeric fields: format and constraints
examples.description: Enter a decimal, then try invalid text and leave the field. Compare the editable draft with the accepted numeric value and its formatted copy.

examples.title: Date fields: entry and display formats
examples.description: Type domani and leave the field. Compare the long and short Italian date formats: they represent the same civil date.

examples.title: Time fields: entry and display formats
examples.description: Change hours and minutes, then leave the field. Compare the second view; the stored value is a civil time, not a timestamp.

examples.title: Search a list and select a value
examples.description: Search for a delivery caption and select it. The second field follows; the readout contains its code rather than the displayed caption.

examples.title: Load choices with a browser callback
examples.description: Search for Sample 02 and choose a result. The browser callback reads a local Bag; the selected code appears in both fields without a server call.

examples.title: Combine free text and suggestions
examples.description: Choose a suggested city, then enter a city outside the list. Both are accepted: suggestions assist free text rather than restricting it.

examples.title: Checkbox group: select several values
examples.description: Select several channels, then clear them all. Compare the comma-separated codes with the null value produced by an empty selection.

examples.title: Inline and popup calendars
examples.description: Choose a day in the inline calendar, then open the popup calendar. Both calendars and the text field follow the same date.

examples.title: Validate required values and text length
examples.description: Enter a one-character name and leave the field. The invalid draft stays visible while the accepted value below remains unchanged; correct it to two or more characters.

examples.title: Arrange fields with formlet
examples.description: Switch between one and two columns. The same fields move without losing their values; the note keeps its own label-position override.

examples.title: Show a boolean as a switch
examples.description: Click the switch or focus it and press Space. The ordinary checkbox follows the same boolean; compare read-only and disabled behavior.

examples.title: Buttons: icons, labels and commands
examples.description: Confirm the first command, then click the delayed command several times quickly. Its result reports one execution for the burst of clicks.

examples.title: Toggle buttons and selection state
examples.description: Toggle Enabled and compare its checkbox. Then try Read only and Disabled: the command's state and whether you can edit it are separate concerns.

examples.title: Dropdown buttons and command menus
examples.description: Open Export and choose CSV. Repeat with Shift held: the command also becomes the main action. The unavailable item cannot execute.

examples.title: Validation rules, warnings and callbacks
examples.description: Try an empty name, quantity 11 and a malformed email. Compare drafts with Accepted Data, then make the email warning blocking and retry.

examples.title: Browse hierarchical Data with a tree
examples.description: Expand Catalog to request its children, then select a row. Add or rename a document and watch the tree follow changes in its Bag.

examples.title: Customize tree labels and row styles
examples.description: Select Notes and rename it. The caption changes while its node key and selected path remain stable.
examples.explanation: Use caption attributes and separate open, closed, selected and node classes.

examples.title: Tree icons and computed captions
examples.description: Expand Documents in both trees and toggle the rich caption. Both read the same Bag; the named callbacks choose different labels and icons.
examples.explanation: Use named Logic for computed labels, explicit sanitized HTML and custom icons.

examples.title: Copy tree nodes with drag and drop
examples.description: Drag a document onto Inbox or Projects, then expand that folder. A copy appears there and the original stays put; Locked archive rejects the drop.

examples.title: Load example data and replay field edits
examples.description: Edit the initialized customer, then use Play to fill the separate draft. Clear interrupts playback; editing the draft leaves the original customer untouched.
examples.explanation: foo_data.tytx supplies the customer before rendering; default initializes only the accent. Edit the name to see the binding update.

examples.title: Bind values with absolute and relative paths
examples.description: Compare the same value through an absolute path, a relative path and an anchor. Edit a field and watch only the views bound to that path change.
examples.explanation: Each ^ pointer subscribes its attribute or text to a Data path; = reads once. A datapath makes .paths relative, #nodeId reaches the context of a named node, and ?attr reads an attribute of a Data node.

examples.title: Change the current record with datapath
examples.description: Choose Ada, edit her name, then select Alan and come back. One card follows the selected datapath; each record keeps its own values.
examples.explanation: The card's datapath is itself a pointer. Choosing another record changes the context of every relative pointer below it; the DOM follows without rebuilding the page.

examples.title: Initialize values: defaults and dataSetter
examples.description: Compare the initialized values below. Defaults fill missing values; dataSetter writes explicitly and is then removed from Source. This lesson demonstrates that distinction deliberately.
examples.explanation: dataSetter nodes sit after the controls and in a later branch, yet the first DOM already shows their values. Controls fill an empty path with default or default_value; attr_ writes an attribute on the Data node.

examples.title: Edit shared Data with native fields
examples.description: Edit a field, then leave it. Compare the accepted Data below; enable live editing to see updates while typing.
examples.explanation: Each control's value is a ^ pointer. Editing writes the Data at change, or at every input when live is true; here live itself follows a checkbox.

examples.title: Bind boolean and single-choice values
examples.description: Toggle the checkbox, then choose a radio option. The readout shows the boolean and the selected code stored in Data.
examples.explanation: A checkbox writes true or false. Radio buttons of one group each own a boolean: choosing one writes true there and false in the others.

examples.title: Control styles and visibility from Data
examples.description: Change the color and dimensions, then toggle visibility. Notice that an invisible box still reserves its place in the layout.
examples.explanation: Attributes such as color, background_color, font_size and rounded compose one style attribute and follow the Data. visible hides an element and keeps its space; hidden removes it from the layout.

examples.title: Update SVG from Data
examples.description: Move the controls and watch the drawing change. SVG attributes use the same Data bindings as text and form fields.
examples.explanation: SVG presentation attributes take ^ pointers like HTML attributes. The circle's radius, the bar's width and both fills are Data values edited by native controls.

examples.title: Defer structural updates with freeze
examples.description: Freeze the branch, increment the count and remove an item. The count updates immediately; item removal appears only after Thaw.
examples.explanation: A frozen branch keeps reacting to Data but defers structural DOM work. Removing a child under freeze takes effect at the thaw, which builds the current Source once.

examples.title: Build a form with shared Data
examples.description: Change the registration fields and compare the Data record alongside them. The password and unbound controls are deliberately absent from that summary.
examples.explanation: The same fieldsets as HTML / SVG example 06, with most fields bound to one Data record. The summary beside the form shows the record while you type; it leaves out the password and the daily radio, and the file input, the read-only code and the disabled field are not bound.

examples.title: Bind SVG geometry and color
examples.description: Move the geometry controls and change the color. The same six SVG shapes update through bound attributes without rebuilding the scene.
examples.explanation: The shapes of HTML / SVG example 08 read their size and color from the Data; sliders and a color field change them.

examples.title: A complete page driven by Data
examples.description: Edit the page's bound controls and follow the repeated values in the complete page. Compare this live version with the earlier static page.
examples.explanation: The event page of HTML / SVG example 12 reads its heading from the event Data record, filters the schedule and the speaker cards by speaker through visible, highlights the chosen map stop and opens the FAQ answers from one flag.

examples.title: Calculate a value with dataFormula
examples.description: Change price or quantity and follow the calculated results. Changing VAT alone does not recalculate Gross: its = pointer is read on the next total change.
examples.explanation: The formula runs when a ^ parameter changes and writes its result; a = parameter is read without triggering. _if and _else choose between two results.

examples.title: React to Data changes with dataController
examples.description: Change the name, send a request and try the delayed input. Each section shows a different reason for a controller to run; the counters make those triggers visible.
examples.explanation: A controller runs code for its effects: here it validates a value, counts fired requests, debounces with _delay and ticks a clock with _timing.

examples.title: Organize behavior in a Logic class
examples.description: Change the price and compare the discounted result and change counter. The page declares the fields; two named Logic methods provide the behavior.
examples.explanation: The page module exports Logic beside Page. func names a method; the framework supplies its resolved parameters. Compare the calculation with the change counter.

examples.title: Use short inline expressions
examples.description: Edit the name and score. Short expressions update the greeting and pass/fail message directly from the other attributes of their node.
examples.explanation: An attribute starting with == is an expression over the other attributes of its node. It follows the pointers it reads, like a formula without a result path.

examples.title: Call methods on a Source node
examples.description: Try SET, PUT and FIRE and compare the value with the notification counter. GET reads the stored value, including a silent PUT.
examples.explanation: Each button action calls a method of its Source node. SET notifies observers, PUT writes silently, FIRE fires also with an equal value, FIRE_AFTER fires after a delay.

examples.title: Run a controller from a button
examples.description: Press the first button normally, then with Shift or Alt. Its nested controller receives the click count and modifiers; the other buttons fire Data paths.
examples.explanation: A dataController nested in a button runs once per click, with button_counter and the modifier keys. fire and fire_<name> write a Data path instead of running code.

examples.title: Handle browser and component events
examples.description: Click a chip, type in the field and move over the pointer area. The visible readouts show which event reached each declaring Source node.
examples.explanation: connect_onclick, connect_oninput, connect_onkeydown and connect_onmouseover add one listener each. The handler runs with this set to the declaring node.

examples.title: Combine inputs, calculations and server calls
examples.description: Change quantity and options, then request a quote. The local total follows edits immediately; the last server quote stays visible until the next successful request.
examples.explanation: First compare setters, live editing, radio flags, formulas, SVG and freeze. After c09/c11, revisit the same inputs with a click-only dataRpc: the server quote is a snapshot, errors retain it and a successful retry clears the error.

examples.title: Start and dispose page behavior
examples.description: Compare the startup trace, freeze the branch and remove it. Observe which updates wait for thaw and which cleanup runs on removal.

examples.title: Project attributes and preview HTML
examples.description: Edit the bound value and compare its text, attributes and HTML preview. The preview is sandboxed and does not execute scripts.

examples.title: Publish and subscribe to messages
examples.description: Run the direct controller, then Publish. Both reach the same summary; the independent receivers show where each message was delivered.

examples.title: Exchange messages between frames
examples.description: Send a message to the child, then reply from it. Compare the two logs to see which frame received each message.

examples.title: Confirm actions and target references
examples.description: Run an action directly, then with confirmation. Cancel a question to leave the result unchanged; the reference examples pass an existing Source or DOM object.

examples.title: Run immediate and delayed button actions
examples.description: Click a delayed button several times quickly, then wait. Compare its single grouped execution with the immediate action and native form reset.

examples.title: Transform bound values with pointer expressions
examples.description: Change the number and compare its CSS width and formatted text. The presentation changes; the stored number keeps its type.

examples.title: Calculate a room estimate
examples.description: Change room, guests and nights. Follow the rate, subtotal, discount, total and deposit; Prepare summary captures a snapshot when clicked.
examples.explanation: Follow room rate and extra guests through nightly price, subtotal, long-stay discount, total and deposit. Change one rule and inspect its downstream effects.

examples.title: Export and restore typed Data
examples.description: Edit the sample record, save it as TYTX, change a value and load the saved file. The typed values and nested Bag are restored together.

examples.title: Define and call a server endpoint
examples.description: The page sends price and VAT rate once at startup. The server returns the gross amount, which appears below through a Data binding.
examples.explanation: The page declares with_vat with @endpoint in Python and Page.registerEndpoint in JavaScript. The author attributes of the dataRpc are the arguments; _init=True makes the call when the page starts.

examples.title: Call the server when a value changes
examples.description: Change the quantity several times quickly. A request starts after you pause typing; compare the status and returned quote.
examples.explanation: Each change of the quantity calls the endpoint 500 ms after the last edit. _onCalling and _onResult are inline code that write the status; the latest call wins.

examples.title: Call the server from a button
examples.description: Reserve the unavailable item, then try the protected action. The error messages distinguish an application error from missing authentication.
examples.explanation: Each click calls the endpoint. An exception answers application_error; an endpoint with auth answers not_authenticated on a server that knows no identity. _onError receives the error.

examples.title: Load a remote Source fragment
examples.description: Choose Lamp, Desk or Chair. The server builds the selected detail fragment; the page replaces only that section.
examples.explanation: The section declares remote('details', record_id='^.record_id'). The page builds the fragment with @source in Python and Page.registerSource in JavaScript; each change of the record requests it again.

examples.title: Cache remote fragments
examples.description: Switch from Lamp to Spotlight, then to Chair. The first two share a category, so the mounted-fragment counter stays unchanged until Chair.
examples.explanation: The rules fragment depends on the category of the product. _cachedRemote makes no request when the category is the same; _onRemote is inline code that counts the mounted fragments and writes the status.

examples.title: Fetch Data with dataRemote
examples.description: Compare the live menu with Read current value. Changing the table updates the bound view; the explicit snapshot stays unchanged until you read again.
examples.explanation: The menu path holds a resolver of the endpoint load_menu with cacheTime 5. The ^.menu paragraph reads it: the answer arrives with the Data event. A change of the table loads the menu again.

examples.title: Border regions and splitters
examples.description: Resize Filters and Details while editing the customer. The center takes the remaining space and the summary follows accepted Data.

examples.title: Nested borders and layout designs
examples.description: Resize an outer region, then a region inside the editor. Each borderContainer owns its layout independently.

examples.title: Rounded borders and popups
examples.description: Change the corner radius, then open a date or choice popup. Compare the nested container edges and the controls inside them.

examples.title: Drawers: handles, content and retained Data
examples.description: Close and reopen the four drawers. The workspace gains space while the fields and their Data remain available when you return.

examples.title: Nested regions playground
examples.description: Move one size control, then drag its corresponding splitter. Both update the same dimension; nested levels keep their own sizes.

examples.title: Border events and controllers
examples.description: Open or close a drawer and resize a region. Compare the event counters and payloads to see the notifications received by controllers.

examples.title: Tabs: select, close and retain content
examples.description: Write an invalid one-character customer name, switch tabs and return. The draft remains. Close Notes and compare the retained Data; expand the reference to compare styles.

examples.title: Switch pages in a single stack
examples.description: Use the slider above the stack to visit a demo, edit it and return later. There is one central stack; a visited page keeps its state.

examples.title: Compare desktop and touch themes
examples.description: Compare the theme previews, open a menu and edit a field. Open dialog and floating windows to compare modality while keeping the same controls.

examples.title: Dialog: modal editing
examples.description: Open the dialog and try the background counter: it is blocked until you close the dialog. Edit the title, close and reopen: the draft is retained.

examples.title: Floating: keep the page usable
examples.description: Open the floating window, then use the background counter. Both remain usable. Edit the title and watch the page update; close and reopen to keep the same draft.

examples.title: groupBox: group fields and copy Data
examples.description: Edit the customer, then use the group's copy command. Only that datapath is copied; the note in the other group is excluded. TYTX preserves types.

examples.title: Tray workspace
examples.description: Arrange live cards, select and move groups, change layers, snap to a grid, and restore a saved Data Bag layout.

examples.title: One hierarchical menu, four presentations
examples.description: One hierarchy with icons, separators, checked and disabled, reused in four presentations plus exact opening modifiers.
examples.explanation: Read the instructions above each example. The shared controls update every presentation.

examples.title: Toolbar: groups, priority and overflow
examples.description: Compact toolbar, retained search, indivisible groups, priority overflow and scrolling.
examples.explanation: Use the width slider. Instructions above each example explain what moves and what stays.

examples.title: Vertical icon toolbar
examples.description: Large icons, tooltip, selected state, separators and priority overflow in a narrow rail.
examples.explanation: Use the height slider, select an icon, and open Tools or overflow. Chevrons follow toolbar orientation.

examples.title: Classic menu bar and hierarchy
examples.description: Named top-level menus, nested side-opening submenus, checked and disabled entries.
examples.explanation: Try File → Export → Image and View → Show details.

examples.title: Reactive menu states
examples.description: Shared checked, disabled and hidden bindings in popup and toolbar.
examples.explanation: Shared checked, disabled and hidden bindings in popup and toolbar.

examples.title: FramePane regions and command recipients
examples.description: Five regions, multiple bars, five-field messages and nested frame isolation.
examples.explanation: Five regions, multiple bars, five-field messages and nested frame isolation.

examples.title: Resolver menus and nested Bags
examples.description: Direct resolver, nested Bags, lazy submenus, live states, empty results and retry.
examples.explanation: Direct resolver, nested Bags, lazy submenus, live states, empty results and retry.

examples.title: Complete document workspace
examples.description: Popup and toolbar together, central content, bindings, remote export, confirmation and delay.
examples.explanation: Popup and toolbar together, central content, bindings, remote export, confirmation and delay.

examples.title: FramePane, dialog and floating windows
examples.description: Modal and nonmodal windows around a retained frame, with movement, resize and collapse.
examples.explanation: Compare defaults, collapsed modality, close guards and background interaction.

examples.title: Complete dialog editor
examples.description: A modal framePane with a top toolbar, editable draft and bottom Save/Cancel actions.
examples.explanation: Follow the steps above the editor. Compare the saved document after Save and Cancel; try reset, details, validation and window controls.

examples.title: Joanna appearance review
examples.description: 32px controls / 14px text — forms, tabs, menus, table and windows.
examples.explanation: Compare the three profiles on the same specimen; try focus, disabled states, menus and window controls.

examples.title: Compact appearance review
examples.description: 28px controls / 13px text — forms, tabs, menus, table and windows.
examples.explanation: Compare the three profiles on the same specimen; try focus, disabled states, menus and window controls.

examples.title: Mimi appearance review
examples.description: 24px controls / 12.5px text — forms, tabs, menus, table and windows.
examples.explanation: Compare the three profiles on the same specimen; try focus, disabled states, menus and window controls.

examples.title: Complete floating editor
examples.description: The same editor in a nonmodal floating window, with top toolbar, fields and bottom Save/Cancel.
examples.explanation: Compare with Complete dialog editor using the same gallery theme and colors. Move or collapse the window and edit Background note to verify the page remains usable.

examples.title: Edit source code with CodeMirror
examples.description: Edit the draft and save a snapshot. Keep typing: the live draft changes while the saved version stays unchanged until you save again.
examples.explanation: Use the base editor or the Source composition with a settings drawer. Save copies a draft snapshot in Data.

examples.title: Configure language, wrapping and editor options
examples.description: Open the editor's Options drawer and change wrapping or font size. The draft remains; changing Language and sample intentionally replaces it.
examples.explanation: Use the base editor or the Source composition with a settings drawer. Save copies a draft snapshot in Data.

examples.title: Edit HTML: source, preview and rich text
examples.description: Edit the code, then switch to Preview and Rich text. The three views share one draft; Preview displays the HTML without running its scripts.

examples.title: Edit Markdown: source, preview and rich text
examples.description: Edit a heading and compare Code, Preview and Rich text. The views share the same Markdown; use Code for complex blocks.

examples.title: Edit Typst and generate a PDF
examples.description: Edit the sample document and inspect its preview, then generate the PDF. Compilation runs locally; this example uses bundled fonts and no external includes.

examples.title: Live Source playground
examples.description: Create an item, change its content and remove it. Compare the Source tree and rendered page; removing the animated section also disposes its timer.
examples.explanation: Builder calls create list items. Source mutations update text, color and structure. A setInterval animates an SVG attribute; removing its section disposes the timer. Works in every gallery command and in the static gallery opened from disk.

examples.title: Color Maker: one block, three contexts
examples.description: Open the palette, select Background, Text or Shadow and move a slider. Random changes only the selected block; the three editors use the same method under different datapaths.
examples.explanation: Open the floating palette, select Background, Text or Shadow, and move a slider. Random changes only the selected block. The same RGB method is reused under three independent datapaths.

examples.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes: animate reactive Data
examples.description: Press Step to discover 2, then again to cross out 4. Start animates the same operation; Pause preserves progress and Reset restores the grid while keeping the chosen speed.
examples.explanation: The grid is built once. Every tick calls the same step method as the Step button; that method updates only the Data Bag. Follow one prime and its multiples, change the interval, and reset while running.
